Residue: Still present at d737f7bc for every holder of the wide Arc: (1) publish/retire/retire_permanently remain `pub` (delegated_server_signer/mod.rs:190,202,218) on a type re-exported at lib.rs:316, so they are external-crate API; cd5dbac0's own smallest_fix (publish/retire module-private, retire_permanently pub(crate)) was NOT applied by #911 (31fd0c8a narrowed only the serving value). current_title: A trust-epoch advance the root declines during signing-plane teardown reports the predecessor key as still serving after the signer was retired
evidence: First pass: Declined is now derived from custody's reissue returning Ok(None) (delegated_server_signer/mod.rs:352-359; mcp-re-http-profile/src/custody/mod.rs:198-213), not from a before_kid read. Ok(None) requires issue_if to return Ok, i.e. custody holds a key valid at now (custody/mod.rs:263-270, hold_off :325-332). The signer is emptied by rotate only on Err (delegated_server_signer/mod.rs:306-313), and custody returns Err only when it holds no valid key (custody/mod.rs:267-270, 333-337) - the sole exception is mintable() overflow of now+ttl or the u64 counter (custody/issuance_terms.rs:52-56 via custody/mod.rs:277-278), unreachable at real clock values. So 'signer retired while custody holds a valid key, then Declined' is no longer reachable on the scheduled path. evidence: The TTL-widening outcome cannot occur. (1) The only production caller passes the real clock: app.rs:254 `let startup_now_unix = now_unix();` flows to SigningPlane::materialize (app.rs:600-603). That value can only lag real time (by startup work), and lag shortens the first key's life. (2) Even if the value ran ahead by D, current() now requires nbf <= now (delegated_server_signer/mod.rs:251, 291c9534), and custody mints nbf = the passed now (custody/mod.rs:412-416). The served window is then [nbf, exp), still ttl long, not ttl+D. The value is still a parameter (signing_plane/mod.rs:133,179); two clock readings remain, but neither widens the window.

second_review.reason: The one caller passes a real clock reading taken once (app.rs:254) and used for materialize at app.rs:598-603 (signing_plane is pub(crate), lib.rs:256, so no other caller exists); it can only lag. If it ran ahead by D, custody mints nbf = that now (custody/mod.rs:412-416 per first pass; activation check custody/active_key.rs:128) and current() refuses before nbf (delegated_server_signer/mod.rs:251), so the credential's verifiable window is still exactly ttl - shifted, not widened.

current_statement: The split-fleet behaviour after a counter rollback remains. A long-lived replica refuses any counter below its in-process high_water (signing_plane/mod.rs:263-268) and stops minting (trust_epoch_advance.rs:81-83,95-116). A replica restarted after the rollback has high_water None and mints <base>#<lower> (mod.rs:246-250,269-270). The doc's agreement claim, 'every replica at counter N mints <base>#N regardless of when it started' (mod.rs:231-238), is unqualified. The restart caveat at :240-245 calls a counter-losing store 'a trust-store failure', but it does not state that the fleet then splits into silent and resurrected-epoch replicas. Related, not the same defect: r11 5fc98328eee54d1a (open, owner-ratified premise for this consumer).

evidence: The fact that was missing from the packet is now established in the tree. The PEP signing call site is answering_commitment.rs:80 -> ResponseSigning::window (receipt/mod.rs:88-90) -> signing_window::open -> DelegatedSigningReader::current(now) (signing_window.rs:18-25; reader.rs:45-47). Refusals use the exchange's snapshot or the same open (receipt/artifact.rs:63-68). `now` is a fresh now_unix() per request (app.rs:830), and the window is snapshotted once per exchange (custody/signing_window.rs:20-24). So G1's honest form is now supported: no consumer reaches the key except through current(), which enforces nbf, exp and Terminal (delegated_server_signer/mod.rs:245-254). It is evaluated per exchange against the real clock. The retirement bound is documented at mod.rs:231-244 (8b5e1462a4ea269e, fixed).

second_review.reason: The out-of-packet fact is now established: the PEP signs only through current() per exchange (answering_commitment.rs:80; receipt/mod.rs:88-90; signing_window.rs:18-26), with refusals reusing that exchange snapshot or the same open (receipt/artifact.rs:63-66); current() enforces nbf, exp and Terminal (delegated_server_signer/mod.rs:245-254) against now_unix() per request (app.rs:830). G1's honest form now has its call site.

evidence: Same defect as r11 25d2f7862a1689b1 (false-positive). The mutex is still taken with `.ok()?` (signing_plane/mod.rs:263). It is held only by the rotation thread, since the watch is moved into the worker (rotation.rs:51-55). A panic in the critical section is converted by the supervisor into permanent retirement plus a FATAL log, and the loop ends (rotation.rs:86-99). The 'never mints again and cannot be told' state is therefore never reached without the signer already retired.

current_statement: Anyone who can write the shared Redis epoch key still decides fleet-wide availability, by regression or by advance. current_label refuses any counter below the in-process high_water (signing_plane/mod.rs:263-268). The loop then refuses to mint at all and backs off (trust_epoch_advance.rs:81-83,95-116). Each replica serves its current key to exp, at most ttl later, and then fails closed. Recovery needs the counter restored to or above every replica's high-water mark, or a fleet restart. The module doc now states the dependency for the advance direction (signing_plane/mod.rs:227-229), but nothing bounds or alarms on it beyond eprintln and the unconsumed metrics.

Same defect as r11 a614ba63d4d1b751, adjudicated a duplicate of 68df51dc512a492d (fixed). terminal latch and snapshot are now ONE value: `enum Snapshot {Empty, Active(Arc<..>), Terminal}` behind one RwLock (delegated_server_signer/mod.rs:104-117,135-138); publish tests Terminal under the same write guard it writes through (mod.rs:190-198); retire cannot leave Terminal (:202-210); retire_permanently writes Terminal, dropping any key (:218-223); seconds_to_expiry returns None for Terminal (:178-181). Landed 291c9534. No live key can stay resident behind a terminal retirement: Terminal holds no Arc.

current_statement: Partly corrected. The misleading refusal text is fixed: config_state/delegated_signing.rs:124-133 now says the base alone is NOT the kill switch, and the test at :325-345 pins this. The always-<base>#<counter> claim is now scoped to DelegatedEpochWatch, which exists only when a source is planned (signing_plane/mod.rs:231).
